answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Each proof uses a recursive cipher verifying unique hardware enclave signatures without revealing agent secrets. To prevent swarm proliferation, identity staking imposes exponential capital exhaustion: the marginal cost scales as C = b^n for each spawned instance. This economic gale forces swarm operators over a financial ledge, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks mathematically and economically unviable.
